Subject: CAIQ mapping scope + runtime logs sampling request

Hi Michael —

Thanks for the draft CAIQ crosswalk you sent last week. Our security reviewers had two follow-ups before we mark the control as ‘validated’:

1) We'd like a compact mapping (control -> evidence pointer) that points at runtime artifacts for inference (KV cache, request routing, and tenant isolation). A single spreadsheet column per control with a one-line evidence description is perfect.

2) For a small canary sample, can you provide instructions and a 48-hour window of runtime log samples (redacted) showing request-level tenant ids, model variant routing decisions and a KV cache hit-rate snapshot? We understand there are privacy constraints — we only need pointers and a sampled, redacted log set.

If possible, include a DocuSign link for the evidence access consent (Aurora legal needs a signed consent for sample logs). Also flag any SLA/retention exceptions we should be aware of; the audit team will escalate exceptions to procurement.

Goal is to close the CAIQ submission by EOD Friday. Appreciate a short plan with owners.

Best,
Kristen Park
Head of Security Programs
Aurora Medical

--

Kristen —

Thanks — we can do this. Quick plan below:

- Deliverable 1: Compact CAIQ mapping spreadsheet (control -> one-line evidence pointer) — Michael (owner). Format: single-sheet XLSX, columns: Control ID | Evidence Summary | Artifact name | Owner contact. Will attach CAIQ_mapping_matrix_20270901.xlsx when ready.

- Deliverable 2: Runtime log canary sample — Irene (owner for logs). We will provide a redaction-safe sampling procedure and a zipped sample of 48 hours limited to non-PHI request metadata. See attached runtime_log_sample_instructions.txt.

- Deliverable 3: Evidence bundle & attestations — Marissa (owner). She will assemble the artifact ZIP (caiq_evidence_manifest.zip) with signatures and a short narrative for each mapped control.

- DocuSign: I'll send a pre-populated consent envelope for Aurora to sign. Link will be included in the follow-up.

Notes / SLA exceptions: We have a standard 90-day retention on raw request traces in Hosted. For the sampling window we can provide a timeboxed extract; long-term retention exceptions require approvals (procurement/legal). If Aurora requires that we hold extracts beyond our default retention, that will need a retention carveout (SLA exception).

Timeline: initial attachments + DocuSign link by 14:00 PT today; log sample delivery within 24 hours after signed consent.

Following up with the technical stub for the sampling process. See brief below and attached instructions.

On sampling and redaction:
- We will only export request metadata (timestamp, anonymized_tenant_id, model_variant_tag, routing_decision, kv_cache_hit_flag). No prompt or response content will be exported.
- Anonymization: tenant IDs will be hashed with a one-way salt. We will share the salt under an NDA only if needed; otherwise the audit team can verify patterns without mapping to PII.
- Sample size: 48 hours of traffic for the tenant(s) in scope or a randomized 10% sample across the window to limit volume.
- Delivery: encrypted ZIP (AES-256) delivered via our secure intake portal.

Attachments included: runtime_log_sample_instructions.txt (contains exact grep patterns, sample rate options and redaction checklist).

Please confirm the preferred sampling mode (full 48h vs randomized 10%). If they choose 10%, indicate preferred start time window.

Thanks — I will prepare the extract once we have a signed consent.

Irene Choi
Director, Observability & Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: runtime_log_sample_instructions.txt
